title: Level a production mix in a heijunka box
instruction: load the heijunka box to level the production mix: put one kanban in each of the six pockets so that no two neighbouring pockets hold the same product colour
context: Lean plants level the product mix over a shift (heijunka) instead of running each product in one batch, which smooths demand on upstream processes and inventory; the heijunka box holds one production kanban per time slot. It measures constraint satisfaction: any sequence with no product in two neighbouring slots scores full, so the model must plan rather than copy an order.
setup: The table top is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. A dark heijunka box is fixed across the far side of the bench at x = 34: six square pockets, 5 cm inside, in a row along y at y = 15, 9, 3, -3, -9 and -15, divided by 1 cm walls 1.5 cm tall. Six kanbans (3 cm cubes in their holders, 40 g) stand on a grey tray (5 x 30 cm) at x = 18, grouped by product: red (product A) at y = 12.5, 7.5 and 2.5; blue (B) at -2.5 and -7.5; yellow (C) at -12.5.
scoring: A pocket counts when it holds exactly one kanban (centre inside the pocket, underside within 1 cm of its floor) and each neighbouring pocket also holds exactly one kanban, of a different colour; a neighbour that is empty or holds two kanbans spoils it. Three reds alone in alternate pockets score 0. Score = pockets that count / 6. The start scores 0; loading them in tray order (red, red, red, blue, blue, yellow) scores 0.17; 1.0 for any levelled sequence, for example red, blue, red, yellow, red, blue. Items are judged only by the positions stated above, not by how they are oriented, so one lying on its side counts the same as one standing; anything the rules above don't cover (for example a part dropped off the table) counts neither way unless a penalty above applies to it. On real arms, read each pocket's colour from a top-down photo of the end state.
reset_notes: Stand the kanbans back on the tray in their groups.
fidelity: Approximate. The kanbans are coloured blocks rather than cards in holders, and the heijunka box is a single row of pockets (a real one has a row per product family). The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Kanbans are coloured blocks rather than cards in holders, so they are easier to grip than real cards.
